title: "rush sql"

```{term}
#| include: false
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
```

The `sql` command runs a [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) query directly against
your files, with no import step. Each file becomes a relation named after the
file, so you can refer to it right in the query.

## Usage

```bash
rush sql [options] [<query>] [--] [<file>...]
```

## Queries

Pass a query and the files it uses:

```{term}
rush sql "SELECT mpg, cyl, hp FROM mtcars WHERE hp > 200 ORDER BY hp DESC" \
  mtcars.csv
```

All of DuckDB's SQL is available, including aggregations, window functions,
and common table expressions:

```{term}
rush sql "SELECT cyl,
                 COUNT(*) AS n,
                 ROUND(AVG(mpg), 1) AS avg_mpg,
                 MAX(hp) AS max_hp
          FROM mtcars
          GROUP BY cyl
          ORDER BY cyl" mtcars.csv
```

## Input

### Files and relation names

Each file becomes a relation named after the file name without its extension:
lowercase, with other characters than letters and digits turned into
underscores. A name that starts with a digit gets an `x` in front, so
`2024 Sales.csv` becomes `x2024_sales`.

`rush sql` queries these formats:

| Format | How |
|--------|-----|
| CSV, TSV, and other text | `read_csv_auto()`, which detects the delimiter |
| Parquet | `read_parquet()` |
| JSON, JSON Lines | `read_json_auto()` |
| DuckDB | Attached, so its tables are `name.table` |

DuckDB reads these files itself, so a query on a large Parquet file doesn't
load the whole file into memory. For other formats, use
[`rush run`](run.qmd), or convert the file first with
[`rush convert`](convert.qmd).

```{term}
rush convert -o mtcars.parquet mtcars.csv
rush sql "SELECT cyl, COUNT(*) AS n FROM mtcars GROUP BY cyl ORDER BY cyl" \
  mtcars.parquet
```

### DuckDB databases

A DuckDB database is attached under its name, and its tables are
`name.table`:

```{term}
rush convert -o garage.duckdb mtcars.csv
rush sql "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM garage.mtcars WHERE hp > 200" \
  garage.duckdb
```

### Standard input

Use `-` to read CSV from standard input, as a relation named `stdin`:

```{term}
printf 'item,price,qty\napple,1.20,10\nbanana,0.80,25\ncherry,3.50,5\n' |
  rush sql "SELECT item, price * qty AS total FROM stdin" -
```

### Joining multiple files

Pass multiple files, and join their relations:

```{term}
printf 'cyl,engine\n4,inline\n6,V6\n8,V8\n' > engines.csv
rush sql "SELECT m.mpg, m.hp, e.engine
          FROM mtcars m JOIN engines e ON m.cyl = e.cyl
          WHERE m.hp > 200" mtcars.csv engines.csv
```

## Output

The result is written like that of [`rush run`](run.qmd#output): a table in
the terminal, CSV when piped, and any format with `--output` (`-o`) or
`--output-format` (`-O`):

```{term}
rush sql -o fast.parquet "SELECT * FROM mtcars WHERE hp > 200" mtcars.csv
rush sql -O json "SELECT cyl, COUNT(*) AS n FROM fast GROUP BY cyl" \
  fast.parquet
```

Use `--head` to write only the first rows. Because the result is an ordinary
table, it can be piped into another command, including another `rush`. See
[Pipelines](../pipelines.qmd).

## Dry run

See the script that runs the query:

```{term}
rush sql -n "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM mtcars" mtcars.csv
```

## Help

```{term}
rush sql -h
```

rm -f mtcars.csv mtcars.parquet garage.duckdb engines.csv fast.parquet
